CID site confirms commercial owners formed it for infrastructure tied to the former GM plant redevelopment; the Doraville packet confirms Series 2017A assessment bonds ($53,005,000), planned Series 2022 bonds, and a CID purpose including street/road construction, stormwater and sewage systems, and water — financing 'certain public infrastructure' for the Assembly project. Tax table shows the 25-mill CID levy (S10T/S13T).

description: The Chamblee Doraville Community Improvement District — commercial property owners in the Chamblee-Doraville area taxing themselves for infrastructure and other projects and programs within the district.
note: Edited tail: 'capital projects and services' changed to 'projects and programs' to match the CID's own wording ('goes towards projects and programs important to the district'); Doraville's city page confirms commercial owners pay additional assessments for critical infrastructure. Tax table bills the CID at the adopted 5-mill maximum in Chamblee (S16) and Doraville (S18).

description: The East Metro DeKalb Community Improvement District — commercial property owners in the Wesley Chapel–Panola Road area of east DeKalb, including part of Stonecrest, taxing themselves for public safety and appearance improvements.
note: Kept as-is. Article confirms the Wesley Chapel–Panola Road corridor in East DeKalb, 205+ commercial property owners, and public-safety/curb-appeal priorities; tax table shows E Metro CID at 3 mills in unincorporated DeKalb (S6) and Stonecrest (S15).

description: Now the Metro South CID (formerly Greater Conley CID) — commercial property owners in the Conley “Truckers Alley” logistics area near the I-285/I-675 interchange in south DeKalb, taxing themselves to improve safety and appearance.
note: Kept as-is. MSCID's About page confirms the former Greater Conley CID name, 2016 creation, 'Truckers Alley', the area surrounding the I-675/I-285 interchanges, and its safety/general-appearance mission; its parcel map is credited to Decide DeKalb. DeKalb billing confirmed by the tax table's Metro S CID line at 5 mills in unincorporated DeKalb (S11).

description: The DeKalb side of the Perimeter Community Improvement Districts — commercial property owners in the Perimeter business district in Dunwoody and Brookhaven taxing themselves for transportation and infrastructure projects.
note: Minor edit: 'Perimeter Center business district' trimmed to 'Perimeter business district' to match the fetched FHWA wording ('Perimeter commercial district'). FHWA confirms PCID partnership with Dunwoody, Brookhaven, DeKalb (and Sandy Springs/Fulton), commercial owners paying additional property taxes for transportation and infrastructure; tax table bills Perim-CID at 4 mills in Dunwoody (S2) and Brookhaven (S3).

description: The Tucker-Northlake Community Improvement District — commercial property owners in the Tucker and Northlake business areas and on Lawrenceville Highway taxing themselves for transportation, streetscape, and safety improvements.
note: Edited: replaced 'downtown Tucker' (not in the fetched source) with 'Tucker and Northlake business areas' per the CID's own description, which also covers Lawrenceville Highway from Tucker Industrial Road to Montreal Road and lists transportation/infrastructure, landscaping and streetscapes, and safety initiatives. Tax table: TNL CID at 3 mills (S5 Tucker, S9 unincorporated), distinct from Tucker Summit CID at 4.

description: The Tucker Summit Community Improvement District (formerly Stone Mountain CID) — commercial property owners in Tucker's Mountain Industrial Boulevard area taxing themselves for road projects, landscaping, and security.
note: Kept as-is. CID site confirms the former Stone Mountain CID name, Mountain Industrial Boulevard/Tucker location in DeKalb, self-taxing commercial owners, and funding of roadway updates and repairs, landscaping, and security. Tax table bills it at 4 mills in Tucker (S4) and unincorporated DeKalb (S8).

description: DeKalb County's fire fund levy, which pays for county fire and rescue service. It is charged in unincorporated DeKalb and in every DeKalb city except Atlanta and Decatur.
note: Kept as-is. Verified: 2025 tax commissioner table shows Fire 2.453 in unincorporated and every city column except Atlanta and Decatur (0.000); the 2026 county table shows the same pattern; 2024 fire rate 2.865 appears in the county's millage-history table.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district covering the part of Atlanta that lies in DeKalb. It carries any county levy beyond the countywide general and hospital taxes; since 2025 the county has billed no extra rate here.
note: Edited. The original's claim that the county 'bills a small city-specific rate here for county special-district services' is contradicted by both cited tables: the 2025 Atlanta column is general 11.027 + hospital 0.611 only, and the 2026 table likewise shows no fire, police, designated-services, or bond rate in Atlanta. The 2024 fund mix behind the digest rate is unverifiable, so the rewrite states only what the tables show.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Avondale Estates — a small city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds, on top of the countywide general and hospital taxes.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Avondale's only extra county levy is Police 0.067; 2026 table: police non-basic 0.073 only. 'Avondale Estates' expansion of AVONDALE EST confirmed via the city's official site (DeKalb County). 2024 composition still unpublished at that granularity, hence medium.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Chamblee — a small city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds, on top of the countywide general and hospital taxes.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Chamblee's only extra county levy is Police 0.027; 2026 table: police non-basic 0.030 only.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Clarkston — a city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds, on top of the countywide general and hospital taxes.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Clarkston's only extra county levy is Police 0.639; 2026 table: police basic 0.626 + non-basic 0.061 only.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Decatur — a small city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds, on top of the countywide general and hospital taxes.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Decatur's only extra county levy is Police 0.036; 2026 table: police non-basic 0.039 only.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Lithonia — a city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds and parks designated-services fund.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Lithonia Police 0.662 + Special Svcs 0.155; 2026 table shows the special-services portion in the Parks column (0.149) with police 0.649 + 0.063, confirming the police + parks mix.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Pine Lake — a city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds and parks designated-services fund.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Pine Lake Police 0.756 + Special Svcs 0.155; 2026 table: police 0.742 + 0.073 plus Parks 0.149, confirming the police + parks mix.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Stone Mountain — a small city-specific county levy that goes to DeKalb's police services funds, on top of the countywide general and hospital taxes.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Stone Mountain's only extra county levy is Police 0.051; 2026 table: police non-basic 0.054 only.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Stonecrest. It carries the county's full police-services millage plus the roads designated-services fund, covering county services provided in the city.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Stonecrest Police 5.965 + Special Svcs 0.248 (the roads portion; unincorporated pays 0.500 roads+parks); 2026 table: full police 6.016 + 0.580 plus Roads 0.129 with no parks; 2024 history rates give 6.444 police + 0.480 roads = 6.924, matching the claimed digest rate.

description: DeKalb County's special tax district within Tucker. Property there pays the county's full police-services millage through this district, funding the DeKalb County police service provided in the city.
note: Kept as-is. 2025 table: Tucker Police 5.965, identical to unincorporated; 2026 table: police 6.016 + 0.580, identical to unincorporated; the county's 2024 history rates (5.819 basic + 0.625 non-basic = 6.444) match the claimed digest rate exactly.

description: A Doraville special service district comprising the Assembly development at the city's former GM plant. Its levy pays Doraville's cost of transportation infrastructure serving the redevelopment.
note: Kept as-is. Packet recites Ordinance 2017-02 authorizing the Special Service District Tax 'to pay the City's cost of providing transportation infrastructure services to and specially benefitting' the district, and the district as 'comprising the Assembly development'; tax table ties S13T to the Assembly SSD millage. Caveat: a 2022 amendment in the same packet restates the purpose more broadly as local government services and facilities.

description: A Doraville special service district covering the city's Tank Farm area. Its levy funds road paving and repair in the district and pays debt on the revenue bonds issued for that work.
note: Rewritten with official sourcing: the cited councilmember campaign page is not an allowed source class, so I replaced it with Doraville's adopted budgets. FY26 budget: SSD Tank Farm bond proceeds pay 'construction, repair and maintenance of the roadways within the Special Service District' and 'Tax revenue for Special Service District Tank Farms to pay debt on Revenue Bond, Series 2024'; FY25 budget cites continuous paving of SSD Tank Farm roads. description: A business improvement district formed in 2023 in Atlanta's Little Five Points; commercial property owners tax themselves for cleaning, safety, graffiti removal, parking management, public art, and public-space activation.
note: Kept as-is. L5P page confirms the BID formed November 2023 at a 3.0 initial millage (CID rate dropped to 0), funding litter/solid-waste management, safety and security, parking management, public art, graffiti cleanup, and public-space activation. Tax table lists Ltl 5 Pts BID at 3 mills in DeKalb's Atlanta district (S7B).

description: A special services district covering Dougherty County's unincorporated area. Its levy funds services there — chiefly county police and fire protection, plus street lighting, recreation, animal control, and code enforcement.

WALB (2026) confirms the SSD is the unincorporated area. Kept as-is; service list is from the FY2018 CAFR.

description: A levy on Effingham County's unincorporated area that funds county parks through the county's Parks & Landscapes department.
note: Resolution: 'County parks 0.100', PT-35 SSD district 1, unincorporated only; FY2025 budget shows the parks line only in the unincorporated residents' millage chart. Budget narrative confirms the Parks & Landscapes department was created with the Special Tax District millages, and its park capital items (Sandhill Park, Reddick Field) are Special Tax District-funded. Kept as-is.

description: A levy funding county recreation programs and facilities run by Effingham County's Recreation & Sports Management department. It applies in the unincorporated area and the cities of Springfield and Guyton.
note: PT-35 lists Recreation as an SSD covering districts 1, 2, and 4 (unincorporated and incorporated boxes both checked). FY2025 budget millage charts show the 0.650 recreation line in the unincorporated, Springfield, and Guyton totals but not Rincon's; narrative confirms the Recreation & Sports Management department sits in the Special Tax District as a result of the recreation millage. Kept as-is.

description: A special district levy on Effingham County's unincorporated area that funds the county Public Works department, primarily road maintenance.
note: Description verified; source URL corrected — the submitted first URL contained a stray space ('usgov cloudapi.net') and was dead as written. Resolution: 'County public works, roads 1.250', listed on the PT-35 as SSD 'Public Works, Roads', district 1, unincorporated only. FY2025 budget narrative: Public Works was moved into the unincorporated Special Tax District 'as a result of the roads and recreation millage'; its capital items are labeled 'Public Works (Roads)'.

description: A countywide levy the county adopts for its Hospital Authority. It pays for medical care and hospitalization of indigent and uninsured patients served by the county hospital, Effingham Hospital in Springfield.
note: Resolution verbatim: 'To provide medical care and hospitalization for the indigent, sick, and others entitled to the services of county hospital 1.480'; staff report says the Board sets millage 'for the county and the Hospital Authority'; PT-32.1 jurisdiction 'MEDICAL INDIGENT'. Herald ties the millage to indigent/uninsured care at the Hospital Authority's hospital; effinghamhealth.org confirms Springfield address (459 GA-119). Caveat: the health system now presents as a 501(c)(3), but the county's 2025 resolution still uses 'county hospital'. Kept as-is.

description: A countywide levy collected for the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority, which develops industrial sites and recruits industry to the county.
note: 2025 levy resolution: 'For the industrial authority 2.000'; PT-32.1 taxing jurisdiction 'INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY'. Countywide confirmed by the FY2025 budget's city millage charts showing IDA 2.000 in unincorporated, Rincon, Springfield, and Guyton totals. ECIDA site documents 8,500+ acres of industrial property and its recruitment role; its millage table shows the 2.000 line. Kept as-is.

description: One of three special service districts Effingham County levies on its industrial areas. The extra tax pays for infrastructure serving industrial traffic, such as roundabouts, road widening, and heavier-duty pavement.
note: Resolution names 'Effingham Gateway special service district'; staff report calls Gateway, Research Forest, and I-16 'the three new special industrial districts' at 1.443 each. Herald (which describes the county's three industrial service tax districts without naming them) states the funds 'help pay for infrastructure improvements such as roundabouts, road widening and heavier pavement installations near industrial operations.' No boundary claimed. Kept as-is.

description: One of three special service districts Effingham County levies on its industrial areas. The added tax funds road and infrastructure upgrades for industrial traffic, including roundabouts, widening, and heavier pavement.
note: Resolution names 'Interstate 16 special service district' (PT-32.1 jurisdiction 'Interstate 16 SSD'), one of the staff report's three special industrial districts at 1.443; Herald sources the funded purpose. Footprint not verifiable, so no geography claimed. Kept as-is.

description: A special service district over the Research Forest industrial tract near Rincon, now the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub. The levy pays for infrastructure serving industrial traffic — roundabouts, road widening, heavier pavement.
note: Resolution names 'Research Forest special service district' as one of the three special industrial districts; Herald sources the purpose. OmniTRAX release verbatim: 'a 2,700-acre tract near Rincon, GA', formerly known as the Research Forest, developed as the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub — 'near Rincon' re-verified verbatim this session. description: A special tax district funding Fayette County's ambulance and emergency medical services; it covers the whole county except Peachtree City, which provides its own EMS.

Peachtree City provides emergency medical services to its citizens.' description: A special district levy funding Fayette County fire protection in all of the county except Fayetteville and Peachtree City, which operate their own fire departments.
note: Verified against extracted budget text: the Fire Services fund pays for 'fire prevention and suppression activities for all areas of the County except for the cities of Fayetteville and Peachtree City, which maintain their own fire departments.' Caveat: FY2026 lowers the rate from 3.070 to 2.820 mills; the description states no rate.

description: A countywide special district levy that helps fund Fayette County's 911 emergency communications system, alongside monthly telephone surcharges.
note: Verified against extracted budget text: 'The special tax district provides 911 communications services to all citizens in the county'; millage remains 0.210 mills, and a $1.50 monthly telephone surcharge supplies most remaining revenue.

description: Rome's Business Improvement District, covering downtown. Property owners there pay an extra levy funding marketing, special events, facade grants, and other supplemental services managed by the Downtown Development Authority.
note: Kept as-is. Both pages confirm the downtown service area, the special assessment on property owners/merchants, the funded categories (marketing, special events, facade and sign grants, supplemental services), and administration by the DDA Board of Directors; renewed for a 10-year term beginning 2025. A City of Rome (Floyd County) district appearing under Floyd in the digest.

description: A levy on property in unincorporated Floyd County funding county solid waste services, including staffed remote collection sites where residents drop off household garbage and recyclables.
note: Edited: dropped 'rural' — the county page confirms staffed remote sites with attendants for household garbage and recyclables but says nothing about rural or eligibility. Solid waste millage confirmed by both news sources. The unincorporated scope is the digest's own UNINC designation.

description: A special district levy on property in unincorporated Floyd County funding fire protection by the Rome-Floyd County Fire Department, including firefighter salaries and fire stations.
note: Edited: department's official name is Rome-Floyd County Fire Department (romegafire.gov). Fire millage and its purposes (firefighter salary increases, new fire station) confirmed by All On Georgia and WRGA. The unincorporated scope is the digest's own UNINC designation; no fetched source states the geographic scope, and the county's 2025 millage ads and budget book cover only M&O and fund totals.

description: The South Forsyth Community Improvement District — commercial property owners along Ga. 400 near McFarland Parkway taxing themselves for road, infrastructure, and other improvements in south Forsyth's commercial corridors.
note: Kept as-is. CID site confirms commercial property owners fund street/road, stormwater, transit, parking, and related improvements; Appen Media confirms establishment in 2019, the boundary along Ga. 400 north and south of McFarland Parkway plus nearby corridors, and that residential parcels inside the CID do not pay the tax.

description: Forsyth County's separate fire tax, levied countywide. It funds the Forsyth County Fire Department, which provides fire protection and emergency medical response across the county.
note: Kept; added the county fire department's official page as corroboration. The county's own announcement (fetched via curl; WebFetch blocked) lists the Fire millage separately from M&O and Bond; Wikipedia states the department provides firefighting and EMS countywide, and the county fire page confirms fifteen stations in Forsyth County and structural firefighting/EMS response.

description: A countywide levy funding the Franklin County Industrial Building Authority, the county's economic development agency, which works to grow the county's tax base and create jobs.
note: Edited: 'recruit industry' was not supported — the IBA page confirms industry retention, regional marketing, growing the tax base, and creating jobs, so the description now uses only the verified objectives. County tax office lists the IBA as the only development-type authority supported by property tax; WLHR confirms the formerly separate IBA millage was consolidated into county M&O in 2025, so this digest line may be historical. No single fetched source ties this exact digest line to the IBA, hence medium.

description: The Atlanta BeltLine Special Service District — commercial and multifamily owners in the BeltLine planning area, including Atlanta's DeKalb side, pay an added levy funding completion of the 22-mile trail loop.
note: Kept as-is. BeltLine SSD page confirms payers (commercial and multi-family owners in the BeltLine Planning Area), the three funded activities, and the 22-mile loop completion goal.

description: A business improvement district formed in 2023 in Atlanta's Little Five Points; commercial property owners tax themselves for cleaning, safety, graffiti removal, parking management, public art, and public-space activation.
note: Edited: removed 'patrols' and 'infrastructure upkeep', which the L5PID page does not list; it lists litter removal, safety and security, graffiti cleanup, public art, parking management, traffic calming, and public space activation. Formation (Nov 2023), 3-mill BID alongside the CID reduced to 0, confirmed.

description: The Airport West Community Improvement District: commercial owners in parts of College Park, East Point, Hapeville, Atlanta, and South Fulton near Hartsfield-Jackson fund safety, beautification, wayfinding, transit, and roads.
note: Kept as-is. AACIDs FAQ confirms AWCID is the Fulton district (ASCID is Clayton), the five cities, the 5-mill levy on non-residential property, and the five focus areas (beautification, public safety, signage/wayfinding, transit, transportation infrastructure).

description: The Midtown Improvement District, a self-taxing district of commercial property owners in Midtown Atlanta; managed by Midtown Alliance, its levy funds local capital projects and programs to improve the district.
note: Kept as-is. MID page confirms every claim verbatim: self-taxing district created by Midtown commercial property owners, Midtown Alliance staffing/operations, 5-mill assessment, funding local capital projects and programs.

description: The Buckhead Community Improvement District: non-residential property owners in about 2.5 square miles of Buckhead's commercial core tax themselves for transportation, streetscape, and park projects, including the PATH400 trail.
note: Edited: PATH400 is a multi-use path, not a park, so 'park projects such as PATH400' was reworded. About page confirms 2.5 sq mi, non-residential payers, 3 mills, transportation and streetscape work; homepage confirms park projects (Charlie Loudermilk Park, Park Over GA400) and PATH400 as a multi-use path.

description: The Atlanta Downtown Improvement District, covering about 220 blocks of Downtown Atlanta; property owners in the district tax themselves to fund clean-and-safe services and planning and capital projects.
note: Edited: the Ambassador Force and wayfinding-signage claims could not be verified on the current Downtown Atlanta Inc site (its JS-rendered program pages return no detail), so they were trimmed. Verified: 220-block coverage and CID status (ADID story page), 'Clean, Safe & Served' and 'Planning & Capital Projects' program areas (ADID and programs pages), and the self-taxing CID mechanism (Georgia Trend).

description: The Fairburn portion of the South Fulton Community Improvement District, where commercial and industrial property owners along the I-85/Oakley Industrial corridor tax themselves for freight-access, road, and mobility improvements.
note: Kept as-is; Georgia Trend added to sources as it explicitly confirms the CID includes portions of the City of Fairburn (present tense, not only the planned expansion). Purpose and payer claims verified as in the Oakley row.

description: The Fulton Industrial Community Improvement District, formed in 2010: property owners along the 11-mile Fulton Industrial Boulevard corridor tax themselves for public safety, transportation, infrastructure, and beautification.
note: Kept as-is. CID site confirms 2010 formation, 11-mile corridor, and the public safety / transportation-infrastructure / beautification priorities; Georgia Trend confirms the self-taxation mechanism and 11-mile length.

description: The North Fulton CID (True North 400): commercial property owners along GA 400 between Mansell and McGinnis Ferry roads in Alpharetta, Milton, and Roswell tax themselves for transportation and infrastructure projects.
note: Kept as-is. About page confirms Mansell-to-McGinnis Ferry extent, the three cities, commercial payers, and transportation/infrastructure focus; homepage (added to sources) confirms the Georgia 400 corridor and self-taxing status.

description: The Fulton County portion of the Perimeter Community Improvement Districts: commercial property owners in Sandy Springs' Perimeter area tax themselves for road, pedestrian, bicycle, and transit-connectivity improvements.
note: Kept as-is. FHWA case study confirms the PCIDs span Fulton and DeKalb counties (Sandy Springs, Dunwoody, Brookhaven), commercial owners voluntarily paying additional property taxes, and vehicular/pedestrian/bicycle/transit-access improvements.

description: The Roswell portion of the North Fulton Community Improvement District (True North 400), where commercial property owners along GA 400 tax themselves for transportation and infrastructure projects.
note: Kept as-is. About page confirms the district spans Alpharetta, Milton, and Roswell with commercial payers; homepage (added to sources) confirms the Georgia 400 corridor and self-taxing status.

description: The South Fulton CID, formed in 1999: commercial and industrial owners along the I-85 and Oakley Industrial Boulevard corridors near Fairburn and Union City tax themselves for freight-access, road, and mobility improvements.
note: Kept as-is. Fairburn city page confirms 1999 formation, self-taxing commercial/industrial owners, Oakley/I-85 focus, and freight-access and mobility improvements; Georgia Trend confirms the I-85 and Oakley corridors and portions of South Fulton, Fairburn, Palmetto, and Union City; CID expansion page confirms road/interchange work.

description: The Upper Westside CID: commercial property owners around the Howell Mill Road and Marietta Street corridors in northwest Atlanta tax themselves for sidewalks, trails, public safety, and other infrastructure improvements.
note: Kept as-is. Atlanta magazine confirms the district was originally the Howell Mill CID (2016), centered on the Howell Mill Road and Marietta Street corridors in northwest Atlanta, with sidewalk and rail-trail projects; CID site confirms commercial-owner levy, public safety, and infrastructure. Medium only because the digest-label-to-CID mapping is inferred.

description: Fulton County's levy on the Fulton Industrial Boulevard corridor, its last unincorporated area, funding the municipal-type services the county provides there: police, fire, code enforcement, and business licensing.
note: Kept as-is. FY2026 budget text (extracted locally from the PDF) states Fund 301's municipal-type services 'include police, fire, code enforcement and business license,' financed by a specific annual property tax levy, and that the fund serves the remaining unincorporated area north of I-20 after the 2021 South Fulton annexation; AJC confirms it was the last unincorporated part of Fulton County.

description: The West End Community Improvement District, in which commercial property owners in Atlanta's West End tax themselves to fund public safety, beautification, infrastructure upkeep, and economic development.
note: Kept as-is. CID site verifies every claim: est. 2017, Atlanta's West End, commercial property owner assessments, funding public safety, beautification, infrastructure, and economic development. Confidence stays medium only because the digest row lacks a CID prefix and the mapping to this CID is inferred.

description: A special district levy funding Glynn County fire protection in unincorporated tax districts 3, 4, and 5 — the Ballard/Blythe Island area of the mainland, St. Simons Island, and Sea Island.
note: Kept as-is. County's 2011 millage table confirms district 3 = Ballard/Blythe Island, 4 = St. Simons, 5 = Sea Island, with Fire levied in exactly those three districts; FY25 budget confirms the Fire Fund is funded through the fire millage in the fire tax districts. Caveat: geographic key is the 2011 table; the 2020 Brunswick News per-district list omits fire for Ballard, but the digest name itself pins fire to districts 3,4,5.

description: A special service district levy funding Glynn County emergency medical services. It is charged in Brunswick and most of the unincorporated county, and proceeds go to the county Emergency Medical Services Fund.
note: Kept as-is; corrected the 404 typo Brunswick News URL to the working one, which I fetched. FY25 budget and OpenGov confirm the EMS Fund was created FY20 for EMS services in the EMS tax districts; the article confirms Brunswick, Ballard, St. Simons, Sea Island, and outlying districts pay EMS while Jekyll pays only county M&O.

description: A special service district levy that funds all Glynn County police services — operations and capital of the county police force. Levied on the unincorporated areas outside Jekyll Island; Brunswick is not in the district.
note: Kept as-is; corrected the 404 typo Brunswick News URL to the working one, which I fetched. FY25 budget: Police Fund created FY20 due to the new Police Tax District and 'reflects expenditures for all County police services and includes police capital and operations.' Article: Ballard, St. Simons, Sea Island, and outlying pay the county police tax; Brunswick's list excludes it and Jekyll pays only county M&O.

description: A special tax district covering Sea Island (county tax district 5). Its levy pays half the cost of the Glynn County police substation on Sea Island; the county covers the other half with a transfer from other county funds.
note: Edited: dropped 'insurance premium tax fund' because the FY25 budget contradicts itself — its fund-summary section says the other 50% comes from the Insurance Premium Tax Fund, but the Sea Island Police Fund (272) detail page says it is 'a transfer from the Police Services Fund.' Substation purpose, 50% special-millage share, and district 5 = Sea Island are confirmed by the budget, OpenGov, and the 2011 millage table.

description: A small levy paid in Brunswick and nearly all of unincorporated Glynn County, funding the county Capital Projects Fund — vehicles, equipment, building improvements, and road and drainage projects in its capital plan.
note: Kept as-is; the cited Brunswick News URL was a 404 typo (a37acdaafe170) — corrected to the working URL, which I fetched. FY25 budget: fund created to fund the CIP, 'a small millage is levied'; fund covers vehicles/mowers/HVAC/pool/IT-traffic equipment, and FY25 projects include the Sea Island/Frederica Roundabout and drainage/stormwater work. Article confirms Brunswick pays it while Jekyll (district 6) pays only county M&O.

description: A special district levy funding fire protection in the part of unincorporated Greene County served by Greensboro's municipal volunteer fire department.
